# Kanpeki

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/README.md

# Kanpeki

Accessible and customizable components that you can copy and paste into your apps. Free. Open Source. **Use this to build your own component library**.

## Documentation

Visit https://kanpeki.vercel.app/docs to view the documentation.

## License

Licensed under the [MIT license](/LICENSE.md).

---

# Commit Message Instructions

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/.copilot-commit-message-instructions.md

# Commit Message Instructions

- The commit message should focus on the files that were changed and the changes that were made.
- Use conventional commit message format.
- The commit message should have a short description (50 characters or less) followed by a blank line and then a longer description.
- The short description should be in the format: `<type>(<scope>): <short description>`
  - `type`: The type of change (e.g., feat, fix, docs, style, refactor, test, chore).
  - `scope`: The scope of the change (e.g., component or file name). Include this if the change is specific to a particular part of the codebase.
- `short description`: A brief summary of the change.
- The long description should provide additional context and details about the change.
  - Explain why the change was made.
  - Describe what is being used and why.
  - It should not exceed 100 characters.

## Example

### Commit Message Example

```
feat(auth): add user authentication

Added user authentication using JWT. This includes login, registration, and token verification endpoints.

- Implemented JWT-based authentication.
- Added login and registration endpoints.
- Added middleware for token verification.

Fixes #123
```

### Breaking Change Example

```
refactor(api): update API endpoints

Refactored the API endpoints to follow RESTful conventions. This change affects all existing API calls.

- Updated endpoint URLs to follow RESTful conventions.
- Modified request and response formats.

BREAKING CHANGE: All existing API calls need to be updated to the new endpoint URLs.
```

---

# accordion.mdx

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/accordion.mdx

title: Accordion
description: A vertically stacked set of interactive headings that each reveal a section of content.
  docs: https://react-aria.adobe.com/DisclosureGroup

<ComponentPreview name="accordion-demo" />

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn-ui@latest add @kanpeki/accordion
```

<ComponentSource name="accordion" />

## Anatomy

  <Tabs.Trigger id="single">Single import</Tabs.Trigger>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="multiple">Multiple imports</Tabs.Trigger>
<Tabs.Content id="single">

```tsx
import { Accordion } from "~/components/ui/accordion";

<Accordion.Root defaultExpandedKeys={["item-1"]}>
  <Accordion.Item value="item-1">
    <Accordion.Trigger>Is it accessible?</Accordion.Trigger>
    <Accordion.Content>
      Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.
    </Accordion.Content>
  </Accordion.Item>
</Accordion.Root>;
```

<Tabs.Content id="multiple">

```tsx
import {
  AccordionContent,
  AccordionItem,
  AccordionRoot,
  AccordionTrigger,
} from "~/components/ui/accordion";

<AccordionRoot defaultExpandedKeys={["item-1"]}>
  <AccordionItem value="item-1">
    <AccordionTrigger>Is it accessible?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>
      Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.
    </AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</AccordionRoot>;
```

## Animation

The accordion uses the `--disclosure-panel-height{:css}` CSS variable to animate the height of the content area.

## Customization

If you need to customize the internal padding of the accordion content, you can use the `*:` Tailwind variant to target the content area directly.

```tsx
<Accordion.Content className="*:pb-12">
  Customized padding for the content area.
</Accordion.Content>
```

## API Reference

### Accordion.Root

      name: "allowsMultipleExpanded",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether multiple items can be expanded at the same time.",
      name: "defaultExpandedKeys",
      typeSimple: "Iterable<Key>",
      description:
        "The initial expanded keys in the collection (uncontrolled).",
      name: "expandedKeys",
      typeSimple: "Iterable<Key>",
      description: "The expanded keys in the collection (controlled).",
      name: "onExpandedChange",
      typeSimple: "function",
      type: "(keys: Set<Key>) => void",
      description: "Handler called when the expanded keys change.",
      name: "isDisabled",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether all items are disabled.",

### Accordion.Item

      name: "id",
      required: true,
      typeSimple: "Key",
      description: "The unique key for the accordion item.",
      name: "isDisabled",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether the accordion item is disabled.",
      name: "isExpanded",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether the accordion item is expanded (controlled).",
      name: "defaultExpanded",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description:
        "Whether the accordion item is expanded by default (uncontrolled).",
      name: "onExpandedChange",
      typeSimple: "function",
      type: "(isExpanded: boolean) => void",
      description: "Handler called when the expanded state changes.",

### Accordion.Trigger

      name: "isDisabled",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether the trigger is disabled.",
      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      type: "ReactNode | (values: ButtonRenderProps) => ReactNode",
      description: "The content to display in the trigger.",

### Accordion.Content

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The content to display in the accordion panel.",

title: Alert
description: Displays a callout for user attention.
  docs: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/alert

<ComponentPreview name="alert-demo" />

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/alert
```

<ComponentSource name="alert" />

## Anatomy

  <Tabs.Trigger id="single">Single import</Tabs.Trigger>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="multiple">Multiple imports</Tabs.Trigger>
<Tabs.Content id="single">

```tsx
import { TerminalIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { Alert } from "~/components/ui/alert";

<Alert.Root>
  <TerminalIcon className="size-4" />
  <Alert.Title>Heads up!</Alert.Title>
  <Alert.Description>
    You can add components and dependencies to your app using the cli.
  </Alert.Description>
</Alert.Root>
```

<Tabs.Content id="multiple">

```tsx
import { TerminalIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { AlertRoot, AlertDescription, AlertTitle } from "~/components/ui/alert";

<AlertRoot>
  <TerminalIcon className="size-4" />
  <AlertTitle>Heads up!</AlertTitle>
  <AlertDescription>
    You can add components and dependencies to your app using the cli.
  </AlertDescription>
</AlertRoot>
```

```bash

```

<ComponentSource name="aspect-ratio" />

## Anatomy

```tsx
import { AspectRatio } from "~/components/ui/aspect-ratio";

<AspectRatio ratio={16 / 9}>
  <Image src="..." alt="Image" className="rounded-md object-cover" />
</AspectRatio>;
```

## Examples

### Square

A square aspect ratio component using the `ratio={1 / 1}{:tsx}` prop. This is useful for displaying images in a square format.

<ComponentPreview name="aspect-ratio-square" />

### Portrait

A portrait aspect ratio component using the `ratio={9 / 16}{:tsx}` prop. This is useful for displaying images in a portrait format.

<ComponentPreview name="aspect-ratio-portrait" />

## API Reference

      name: "ratio",
      type: "number",
      typeSimple: "number",
      default: "1 / 1",
      description: "The desired aspect ratio.",

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/autocomplete
```

<ComponentSource name="autocomplete" />

## Anatomy

```tsx
import { Autocomplete } from "~/components/ui/autocomplete";
import { Menu } from "~/components/ui/menu";
import { SearchField } from "~/components/ui/search-field";

<Autocomplete>
  <SearchField /> or <TextField />
  <Menu /> or <ListBox />
</Autocomplete>;
```

# avatar.mdx

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/avatar.mdx

title: Avatar
description: An image element with a fallback for representing the user.

<ComponentPreview name="avatar-demo" />

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/avatar
```

<ComponentSource name="avatar" />

## Anatomy

  <Tabs.Trigger id="single">Single import</Tabs.Trigger>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="multiple">Multiple imports</Tabs.Trigger>
<Tabs.Content id="single">

```tsx
import { UserIcon } from "lucide-react";
import { Avatar } from "~/components/ui/avatar";

<Avatar.Root>
  <Avatar.Image src="https://github.com/fellipeutaka.png" alt="@fellipeutaka" />
  <Avatar.Fallback>FU</Avatar.Fallback>
  <Avatar.Placeholder>
    <UserIcon className="size-6" />
  </Avatar.Placeholder>
</Avatar.Root>;
```

```tsx
import { UserIcon } from "lucide-react";
import {
  AvatarRoot,
  AvatarFallback,
  AvatarImage,
  AvatarPlaceholder,
} from "~/components/ui/avatar";

<AvatarRoot>
  <AvatarImage src="https://github.com/fellipeutaka.png" alt="@fellipeutaka" />
  <AvatarFallback>FU</AvatarFallback>
  <AvatarPlaceholder>
    <UserIcon className="size-6" />
  </AvatarPlaceholder>
</AvatarRoot>;
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
import { Badge } from "~/components/ui/badge";

<Badge variant="outline">Badge</Badge>
```

## Link

You can use the `BadgeStyles` helper to create a link that looks like a badge.

```tsx
import { BadgeStyles } from "~/components/ui/badge";

<Link className={BadgeStyles({ variant: "outline" })}>Badge</Link>
```

# breadcrumb.mdx

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/breadcrumb.mdx

title: Breadcrumb
description: Breadcrumbs display a hierarchy of links to the current page or resource in an application.
  docs: https://react-aria.adobe.com/Breadcrumbs

<ComponentPreview name="breadcrumb-demo" />

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/breadcrumb
```

<ComponentSource name="breadcrumb" />

## Anatomy

  <Tabs.Trigger id="single">Single import</Tabs.Trigger>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="multiple">Multiple imports</Tabs.Trigger>
<Tabs.Content id="single">

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from "~/components/ui/breadcrumb";
import { Link } from "~/components/ui/link";

<Breadcrumb.Root>
  <Breadcrumb.Item>
    <Link />
  </Breadcrumb.Item>
  <Breadcrumb.Separator />
  <Breadcrumb.Item>
    <Breadcrumb.Ellipsis />
  </Breadcrumb.Item>
  <Breadcrumb.Separator />
  <Breadcrumb.Item>
    <Link />
  </Breadcrumb.Item>
</Breadcrumb.Root>;
```

<Tabs.Content id="multiple">

```tsx
import {
  BreadcrumbRoot,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
  BreadcrumbEllipsis,
  BreadcrumbPage,
} from "~/components/ui/breadcrumb";
import { Link } from "~/components/ui/link";

<BreadcrumbRoot>
  <BreadcrumbItem>
    <Link />
  </BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbSeparator />
  <BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbEllipsis />
  </BreadcrumbItem>
  <BreadcrumbSeparator />
  <BreadcrumbItem>
    <Link />
  </BreadcrumbItem>
</BreadcrumbRoot>;
```

## Examples

### Custom Separator

Use a custom component as `children` for `<BreadcrumbSeparator />{:tsx}` to create a custom separator.

<ComponentPreview name="breadcrumb-custom-separator-demo" />

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from "~/components/ui/breadcrumb";
import { SlashIcon } from "lucide-react"; // [!code highlight]

<Breadcrumb.Root>
  {/* ... */}
  {/* [!code highlight:3] */}
  <Breadcrumb.Separator>
    <Icons.Slash className="size-4" />
  </Breadcrumb.Separator>
  {/* ... */}
</Breadcrumb.Root>;
```

### Dropdown

You can compose `<BreadcrumbItem />{:tsx}` with a `<Menu />{:tsx}` to create a dropdown in the breadcrumb.

<ComponentPreview name="breadcrumb-dropdown-demo" />

```tsx
import { Button } from "react-aria-components"; // [!code highlight]
import { Breadcrumb } from "~/components/ui/breadcrumb"; // [!code highlight]
import { Menu } from "~/components/ui/menu"; // [!code highlight]
import { LinkStyles } from "~/components/ui/link"; // [!code highlight]
import { Popover } from "~/components/ui/popover"; // [!code highlight]

<Breadcrumb.Root>
  {/* ... */}
  <Breadcrumb.Item>
    <Menu.Root>
      <Button className={LinkStyles({ variant: "default" })}>Components</Button>

      <Popover.Content>
        <Popover.Arrow />

        <Menu.Content>
          <Menu.Item>Documentation</Menu.Item>
          <Menu.Item>Themes</Menu.Item>
          <Menu.Item>GitHub</Menu.Item>
        </Menu.Content>
      </Popover.Content>
    </Menu.Root>
  </Breadcrumb.Item>
  {/* ... */}
</Breadcrumb.Root>;
```

### Collapsed

There's a `<BreadcrumbEllipsis />{:tsx}` component to show a collapsed state when the breadcrumb is too long.

<ComponentPreview name="breadcrumb-collapsed-demo" />

```tsx
import { Breadcrumb } from "~/components/ui/breadcrumb"; // [!code highlight]

<Breadcrumb.Root>
  {/* ... */}
  <Breadcrumb.Item>
    {/* [!code highlight] */}
    <Breadcrumb.Ellipsis className="size-4" />
  </Breadcrumb.Item>
  {/* ... */}
</Breadcrumb.Root>;
```

## API Reference

### Breadcrumb.Root

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The breadcrumb items.",
      name: "isDisabled",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether the breadcrumbs are disabled.",
      name: "onAction",
      typeSimple: "function",
      type: "(key: Key) => void",
      description: "Handler called when a breadcrumb item is pressed.",

### Breadcrumb.Item

      name: "id",
      typeSimple: "Key",
      description: (
        <>
          A unique id for the breadcrumb, which will be passed to{" "}
          <Code>onAction</Code> when the breadcrumb is pressed.
        </>
      ),
      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      type: "ReactNode | (values: BreadcrumbRenderProps) => ReactNode",
      description: "The content of the breadcrumb item.",

### Breadcrumb.Separator

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "Custom separator content. Defaults to a chevron icon.",

### Breadcrumb.Ellipsis

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description:
        "Custom ellipsis content. Defaults to a horizontal dots icon.",

# button-group.mdx

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/button-group.mdx

title: Button Group
description: A container that groups related buttons together with consistent styling.
  docs: https://react-aria.adobe.com/Group

<ComponentPreview name="button-group-demo" />

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/button-group
```

<Step>Install the following dependencies:</Step>

```bash
npm install radix-ui
```

<ComponentSource name="button-group" />

## Anatomy

  <Tabs.Trigger id="single">Single import</Tabs.Trigger>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="multiple">Multiple imports</Tabs.Trigger>
<Tabs.Content id="single">

```tsx
import { Button } from "~/components/ui/button";
import { ButtonGroup } from "~/components/ui/button-group";

<ButtonGroup.Root>
  <Button>Button 1</Button>
  <Button>Button 2</Button>
</ButtonGroup.Root>;
```

<Tabs.Content id="multiple">

```tsx
import { Button } from "~/components/ui/button";
import { ButtonGroupRoot } from "~/components/ui/button-group";

<ButtonGroupRoot>
  <Button>Button 1</Button>
  <Button>Button 2</Button>
</ButtonGroupRoot>;
```

## Accessibility

- The `ButtonGroup.Root` component has the `role` attribute set to `group`.
- Use <Keyboard>Tab</Keyboard> to navigate between the buttons in the group.
- Use `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` to label the button group.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup.Root aria-label="Button group">
  <Button>Button 1</Button>
  <Button>Button 2</Button>
</ButtonGroup.Root>
```

## ButtonGroup vs ToggleGroup

- Use the `ButtonGroup` component when you want to group buttons that perform an action.
- Use the `ToggleGroup` component when you want to group buttons that toggle a state.

## Examples

### Orientation

Set the `orientation` prop to change the button group layout.

<ComponentPreview name="button-group-orientation-demo" />

### Size

Control the size of buttons using the `size` prop on individual buttons.

<ComponentPreview name="button-group-size-demo" />

### Nested

Nest `<ButtonGroup>` components to create button groups with spacing.

<ComponentPreview name="button-group-nested-demo" />

### Separator

The `ButtonGroupSeparator` component visually divides buttons within a group.

Buttons with variant `outline` do not need a separator since they have a border. For other variants, a separator is recommended to improve the visual hierarchy.

<ComponentPreview name="button-group-separator-demo" />

### Split

Create a split button group by adding two buttons separated by a `ButtonGroupSeparator`.

<ComponentPreview name="button-group-split-demo" />

### Input

Wrap an `Input` component with buttons.

<ComponentPreview name="button-group-input-demo" />

### Input Group

Wrap an `InputGroup` component to create complex input layouts.

<ComponentPreview name="button-group-input-group-demo" />

### Dropdown Menu

Create a split button group with a `DropdownMenu` component.

<ComponentPreview name="button-group-dropdown-demo" />

### Select

Pair with a `Select` component.

<ComponentPreview name="button-group-select-demo" />

### Popover

Use with a `Popover` component.

<ComponentPreview name="button-group-popover-demo" />

## API Reference

### ButtonGroup

The `ButtonGroup` component is a container that groups related buttons together with consistent styling.

      name: "orientation",
      type: '"horizontal" | "vertical"',
      typeSimple: "enum",
      default: '"horizontal"',
      description: "The orientation of the button group.",

```tsx
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button>Button 1</Button>
  <Button>Button 2</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

Nest multiple button groups to create complex layouts with spacing. See the [nested](#nested) example for more details.

```tsx
<ButtonGroup>
  <ButtonGroup />
  <ButtonGroup />
</ButtonGroup>
```

### ButtonGroupSeparator

The `ButtonGroupSeparator` component visually divides buttons within a group.

      name: "orientation",
      type: '"horizontal" | "vertical"',
      typeSimple: "enum",
      default: '"vertical"',
      description: "The orientation of the separator.",

```tsx
<ButtonGroup>
  <Button>Button 1</Button>
  <ButtonGroupSeparator />
  <Button>Button 2</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### ButtonGroupText

Use this component to display text within a button group.

      name: "render",
      type: "React.ReactElement | ((props: React.HTMLAttributes<any>) => React.ReactElement)",
      typeSimple: "ReactElement | function",
      description: "Render as a custom element.",

```tsx
<ButtonGroup>
  <ButtonGroupText>Text</ButtonGroupText>
  <Button>Button</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

Use the `render` prop to render a custom element, for example a label.

```tsx
import { ButtonGroupText } from "~/components/ui/button-group";
import { Label } from "~/components/ui/label";

export function ButtonGroupTextDemo() {
  return (
    <ButtonGroup>
      <ButtonGroupText render={<Label htmlFor="name" />}>Text</ButtonGroupText>
      <Input placeholder="Type something here..." id="name" />
    </ButtonGroup>
  );
}
```

---

title: Button
description: Displays a button or a component that looks like a button.
  docs: https://react-aria.adobe.com/Button

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/button
```

<ComponentSource name="button" />

## Anatomy

```tsx
import { Button } from "~/components/ui/button";

<Button variant="outline">Button</Button>;
```

## Examples

### Sizes

<ComponentPreview name="button-sizes-demo" />

### Custom Variants

<ComponentPreview name="button-variants-demo" />

### Icon

<ComponentPreview name="button-icon-demo" />

<Card.Root className="mt-6">
  <Card.Header className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <Card.Action className="grid place-content-center rounded-full bg-secondary/80 p-2">
      <AlertIcon variant="warning" className="text-amber-400" />
    </Card.Action>

    <Card.Title>Icon-only buttons need accessible labels.</Card.Title>

  </Card.Header>
  <Card.Content>
    <Card.Description>
      Choose your preferred approach:

      ```tsx
      // Option 1: aria-label (concise)
      // [!code word:aria-label="Search"]
      <Button size="icon" aria-label="Search">
        <SearchIcon />
      </Button>

      // Option 2: visually hidden text
      <Button size="icon">
        <SearchIcon />
        // [!code highlight]
        <span className="sr-only">Search</span>
      </Button>
      ```

      Both work identically. Use `aria-label` for brevity or `sr-only` for visibility in your code.
    </Card.Description>

  </Card.Content>
</Card.Root>

## API Reference

# carousel.mdx

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/carousel.mdx

title: Carousel
description: A carousel with motion and swipe built using Embla.
  docs: https://www.embla-carousel.com/get-started/react
  api: https://www.embla-carousel.com/api

<ComponentPreview name="carousel-demo" />

## About

The carousel component is built using the [Embla Carousel](https://www.embla-carousel.com/) library.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/carousel
```

<Step>Install the following dependencies:</Step>

```bash
npm install embla-carousel-react
```

<ComponentSource name="carousel" />

## Anatomy

```tsx
import { Carousel } from "~/components/ui/carousel";

<Carousel.Root>
  <Carousel.Content>
    <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
  </Carousel.Content>
  <Carousel.Previous />
  <Carousel.Next />
</Carousel.Root>;
```

## Examples

### Sizes

To set the size of the items, you can use the `basis{:tsx}` utility class on the `<Carousel.Item>{:tsx}`.

<ComponentPreview name="carousel-size-demo" />

```tsx
// [!code word:basis-1/3]
// 33% of the carousel width.
<Carousel.Root>
  <Carousel.Content>
    <Carousel.Item className="basis-1/3">...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item className="basis-1/3">...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item className="basis-1/3">...</Carousel.Item>
  </Carousel.Content>
</Carousel.Root>
```

```tsx
// [!code word:md\:basis-1/2]
// [!code word:lg\:basis-1/3]
// 50% on small screens and 33% on larger screens.
<Carousel.Root>
  <Carousel.Content>
    <Carousel.Item className="md:basis-1/2 lg:basis-1/3">...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item className="md:basis-1/2 lg:basis-1/3">...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item className="md:basis-1/2 lg:basis-1/3">...</Carousel.Item>
  </Carousel.Content>
</Carousel.Root>
```

### Spacing

To set the spacing between the items, we use a `pl-[VALUE]{:tsx}` utility on the `<Carousel.Item>{:tsx}` and a negative `-ml-[VALUE]{:tsx}` on the `<Carousel.Content>{:tsx}`.

<Alert.Root>
  <AlertIcon variant="info" />
  <Alert.Description>
    **Why:** I tried to use the `gap{:tsx}` property or a `grid{:tsx}` layout on the `<Carousel.Content>{:tsx}` but it required a lot of math and mental effort to get the spacing right. I found `pl-[VALUE]{:tsx}` and `-ml-[VALUE]{:tsx}` utilities much easier to use.

    You can always adjust this in your own project if you need to.

  </Alert.Description>
</Alert.Root>

<ComponentPreview name="carousel-spacing-demo" />

```tsx
// [!code word:-ml-4]
// [!code word:pl-4]
<Carousel.Root>
  <Carousel.Content className="-ml-4">
    <Carousel.Item className="pl-4">...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item className="pl-4">...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item className="pl-4">...</Carousel.Item>
  </Carousel.Content>
</Carousel.Root>
```

```tsx
// [!code word:-ml-2]
// [!code word:md\:-ml-4]
// [!code word:pl-2]
// [!code word:md\:pl-4]
<Carousel.Root>
  <Carousel.Content className="-ml-2 md:-ml-4">
    <Carousel.Item className="pl-2 md:pl-4">...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item className="pl-2 md:pl-4">...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item className="pl-2 md:pl-4">...</Carousel.Item>
  </Carousel.Content>
</Carousel.Root>
```

### Orientation

Use the `orientation{:tsx}` prop to set the orientation of the carousel.

<ComponentPreview name="carousel-orientation-demo" />

```tsx
// [!code word:orientation]
<Carousel.Root orientation="vertical | horizontal">
  <Carousel.Content>
    <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
  </Carousel.Content>
</Carousel.Root>
```

## Options

You can pass options to the carousel using the `opts{:tsx}` prop. See the [Embla Carousel docs](https://www.embla-carousel.com/api/options/) for more information.

```tsx
<Carousel.Root
  // [!code highlight:4]
  opts={{
    align: "start",
    loop: true,
  }}
>
  <Carousel.Content>
    <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
    <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
  </Carousel.Content>
</Carousel.Root>
```

## API

Use a state and the `setApi{:tsx}` prop to get an instance of the carousel API.

<ComponentPreview name="carousel-api-demo" />

```tsx
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import { Carousel, type CarouselApi } from "~/registry/ui/carousel"; // [!code highlight]

export function Example() {
  const [api, setApi] = useState<CarouselApi>(); // [!code highlight]
  const [current, setCurrent] = useState(0);
  const [count, setCount] = useState(0);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!api) {
      return;
    }

    setCount(api.scrollSnapList().length);
    setCurrent(api.selectedScrollSnap() + 1);

    api.on("select", () => {
      setCurrent(api.selectedScrollSnap() + 1);
    });
  }, [api]);

  return (
    // [!code highlight]
    <Carousel.Root setApi={setApi}>
      <Carousel.Content>
        <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
        <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
        <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
      </Carousel.Content>
    </Carousel.Root>
  );
}
```

## Events

You can listen to events using the api instance from `setApi{:tsx}`.

```tsx
import type { CarouselApi } from "~/components/ui/carousel"; // [!code highlight]

export function Example() {
  // [!code highlight:11]
  const [api, setApi] = useState<CarouselApi>();

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!api) {
      return;
    }

    api.on("select", () => {
      // Do something on select.
    });
  }, [api]);

  return (
    // [!code highlight]
    <Carousel.Root setApi={setApi}>
      <Carousel.Content>
        <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
        <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
        <Carousel.Item>...</Carousel.Item>
      </Carousel.Content>
    </Carousel.Root>
  );
}
```

See the [Embla Carousel docs](https://www.embla-carousel.com/api/events/) for more information on using events.

## Plugins

You can use the `plugins{:tsx}` prop to add plugins to the carousel.

```tsx
import Autoplay from "embla-carousel-autoplay"; // [!code highlight]

export function Example() {
  return (
    <Carousel.Root
      // [!code highlight:5]
      plugins={[
        Autoplay({
          delay: 2000,
        }),
      ]}
    >
      // ...
    </Carousel.Root>
  );
}
```

<ComponentPreview name="carousel-plugin-demo" />

See the [Embla Carousel docs](https://www.embla-carousel.com/api/plugins/) for more information on using plugins.

# Component Documentation Guidelines

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/CLAUDE.md

# Component Documentation Guidelines

Guidelines for creating component documentation in the Kanpeki project.

## File Structure

Component documentation files are located in `src/content/docs/components/` and follow this pattern:

- `<component-name>.mdx` - Main documentation file
- Example components in `src/registry/examples/<component-name>/`
- Registry entries in `src/registry/examples/<component-name>/_registry.ts`

**Important**: After creating, updating, or deleting any component or file inside `src/registry/`:

1. Validate your changes:

   ```bash
   bun run registry:validate
   ```

2. If validation passes, rebuild the registry:
   ```bash
   bun run registry:build
   ```

This ensures your changes follow naming conventions before rebuilding the registry.

## MDX Frontmatter

```yaml
---
title: ComponentName
description: Brief description of what the component displays or does.
links:
  docs: https://react-aria.adobe.com/ComponentName
  api: https://react-aria.adobe.com/ComponentName#props
---
```

**Notes**:

- `title` (required): Max 32 characters
- `description` (required): Max 256 characters
- `links` (optional): Object with `docs` and/or `api` URLs

### Documentation Link Suggestions

When adding the `links.docs` field, verify the URL exists before including it. Common documentation sources:

- **React Aria Components**: `https://react-aria.adobe.com/ComponentName`
- **Base UI**: `https://base-ui.com/react/components/component-name`

You can link to any relevant documentation - these are just common options.

### Verifying Documentation Links

Before adding documentation links, verify they exist using these tools:

**React Aria Components**

- Use the `react-aria` MCP server to search component docs
- If not installed: `claude mcp add react-aria npx @react-aria/mcp@latest`
- MCP docs: https://react-aria.adobe.com/mcp

**Base UI**

- Use WebFetch with their llms.txt: `https://base-ui.com/llms.txt`
- Use the Context7 MCP server to search Base UI documentation
- Example: `mcp__context7__resolve-library-id` then `mcp__context7__get-library-docs`
- Or search the docs directly

**Any documentation**

- Use WebFetch or WebSearch tools to verify the URL exists

## Document Structure

### 1. Preview (First Section)

Start with a component preview showcasing the default/demo example:

```mdx
<ComponentPreview name="component-demo" />
```

**Important**: `ComponentPreview` only accepts a `name` prop, no `description` prop.

### 2. Installation

Use `Tabs.Root`, `Tabs.List`, `Tabs.Trigger`, and `Tabs.Content` (NOT the singular `Tabs` component):

````mdx
## Installation

<Tabs.Root>

<Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="cli">CLI</Tabs.Trigger>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="manual">Manual</Tabs.Trigger>
</Tabs.List>
<Tabs.Content id="cli">

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/component-name
```
````

<ComponentSource name="component-name" />

````

**Key patterns**:
- Use `npm` for package manager commands (not `bun`)
- CLI command: `npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/component-name`
- Manual installation uses `<Steps>` component
- First step: "Copy and paste the following code into your project."
- Second step: "Update the import paths to match your project setup."

### 3. Anatomy

Use `## Anatomy` (NOT `## Usage`):

```mdx
## Anatomy

```tsx
import { Component } from "~/components/ui/component";

<Component />;
````

````

For components with multiple import patterns, use tabs:

```mdx
## Anatomy

<Tabs.Root>

<Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="single">Single import</Tabs.Trigger>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="multiple">Multiple imports</Tabs.Trigger>
</Tabs.List>
<Tabs.Content id="single">

```tsx
import { Component } from "~/components/ui/component";

<Component.Root>
  <Component.Item />
</Component.Root>;
````

<Tabs.Content id="multiple">

```tsx
import { ComponentRoot, ComponentItem } from "~/components/ui/component";

<ComponentRoot>
  <ComponentItem />
</ComponentRoot>;
```

````

### 4. Examples

**Important**: Do NOT repeat the demo example shown at the top of the page.

Each example should:
- Have a descriptive heading (e.g., `### File`, `### Disabled`, `### With Label`)
- Use `<ComponentPreview name="component-example-name" />`

```mdx
## Examples

### Variant Name

<ComponentPreview name="component-variant" />
````

## Inline Code Syntax Highlighting

When referencing components, props, or attributes in prose, use the `{:tsx}` suffix for syntax highlighting:

**Component references:**

- ✅ `<Component>{:tsx}` or `<Component.Item>{:tsx}`
- ❌ `Component` or `Component.Item`

**Props and attributes:**

- ✅ `variant{:tsx}`, `isInvalid{:tsx}`, `data-invalid{:tsx}`, `aria-label{:tsx}`
- ❌ `variant`, `isInvalid`, `data-invalid`, `aria-label`

**Prop values:**

- ✅ `variant="primary"{:tsx}`, `role="dialog"{:tsx}`
- ❌ `variant="primary"`, `role="dialog"`

Examples:

```mdx
Use `<TextField>{:tsx}` with the `isInvalid{:tsx}` prop.

Set `orientation="horizontal"{:tsx}` on `<Field.Root>{:tsx}`.

Add `aria-label{:tsx}` for accessibility.
```

**Exception:** Do NOT use `{:tsx}` in code blocks (fenced with triple backticks) or prop names within `<PropsTable>` data.

## Alert/Callout Pattern

Use `<Alert.Root>` with `<AlertIcon />` (NOT `<Callout>`):

```mdx
<Alert.Root>
  <AlertIcon variant="info" />
  <Alert.Description>
    Your message here with [markdown links](/path).
  </Alert.Description>
</Alert.Root>
```

For warnings:

```mdx
<Alert.Root variant="warning">
  <AlertIcon variant="warning" />
  <Alert.Description>Warning message here.</Alert.Description>
</Alert.Root>
```

## Example Component Files

Example files in `src/registry/examples/<component-name>/`:

### File Naming

- **Files must end with `-demo.tsx` suffix**: `component-name-demo.tsx`, `component-name-variant-demo.tsx`
- Use kebab-case for all parts: `button-demo.tsx`, `input-disabled-demo.tsx`
- Export as named function with `Demo` suffix: `export function ComponentNameVariantDemo() {}`
- Function name must match filename in PascalCase:
  - `button-demo.tsx` → `export function ButtonDemo()`
  - `input-disabled-demo.tsx` → `export function InputDisabledDemo()`
  - `input-otp-demo.tsx` → `export function InputOTPDemo()` (preserves acronyms like OTP, API, URL)

### Import Paths

Always use `~/registry/` prefix for component imports:

```tsx
import { Component } from "~/registry/ui/component";
import { Label } from "~/registry/ui/label";
```

### Example Pattern

```tsx
import { Input } from "~/registry/ui/input";

export function InputDemo() {
  return <Input type="email" placeholder="Email" />;
}
```

### Registry Validation

Before committing, validate that your examples follow the required structure:

```bash
bun run registry:validate
```

**What it validates:**

1. ✅ Each component folder has `_registry.ts`
2. ✅ Each folder contains at least one `.tsx` file
3. ✅ All `.tsx` files end with `-demo.tsx`
4. ✅ Each file exports exactly one function
5. ✅ Function names end with `Demo` suffix
6. ✅ Function names match filenames (PascalCase)

**Example errors:**

```bash
📦 button:
   • File "button-icon.tsx" must have -demo.tsx suffix (e.g., "button-icon-demo.tsx")
   • File "button-icon-demo.tsx" exports function "ButtonIcon" which must end with "Demo" suffix. Expected: "ButtonIconDemo"
```

**Fix the errors, then run:**

- `bun run registry:validate` - Ensure all errors are fixed
- `bun run registry:build` - Rebuild the registry

## Registry Entry

Update `_registry.ts` in the examples folder:

```ts
import type { RegistryItem } from "shadcn/schema";

export const componentExamples: RegistryItem[] = [
  {
    name: "component-demo",
    type: "registry:example",
    registryDependencies: ["@kanpeki/component"],
    files: [
      {
        path: "src/registry/examples/component/component-demo.tsx",
        type: "registry:example",
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    name: "component-variant",
    type: "registry:example",
    registryDependencies: ["@kanpeki/component", "@kanpeki/other-dependency"],
    files: [
      {
        path: "src/registry/examples/component/component-variant.tsx",
        type: "registry:example",
      },
    ],
  },
];
```

## Common Patterns

### API Reference Section

If needed, add API documentation using `<PropsTable>`:

```mdx
## API Reference

<PropsTable
  data={[
    {
      name: "variant",
      required: false,
      typeSimple: "enum",
      type: '"default" | "outline"',
      default: '"default"',
      description: "The visual style.",
    },
  ]}
/>
```

### Browser Compatibility Warnings

```mdx
<Alert.Root variant="warning">
  <AlertIcon variant="warning" className="size-4" />
  <Alert.Description>
    The `property-name` CSS property is not supported in all browsers. See the
    [browser compatibility](https://caniuse.com/link) table for more
    information.
  </Alert.Description>
</Alert.Root>
```

### Icon-Only Components

```mdx
<Card.Root className="mt-6">
  <Card.Header className="flex items-center gap-2">
    <Card.Action className="grid place-content-center rounded-full bg-secondary/80 p-2">
      <AlertIcon variant="warning" className="text-amber-400" />
    </Card.Action>
    <Card.Title>Title here</Card.Title>
  </Card.Header>
  <Card.Content>
    <Card.Description>Content here</Card.Description>
  </Card.Content>
</Card.Root>
```

## Checklist

- [ ] Frontmatter with title, description, and docs link
- [ ] Initial `<ComponentPreview>` with demo
- [ ] Installation section with CLI and Manual tabs
- [ ] Anatomy section (not Usage)
- [ ] Examples section (without repeating demo)
- [ ] Example components created in `src/registry/examples/`
- [ ] **All example files end with `-demo.tsx` suffix**
- [ ] **All exported functions end with `Demo` suffix**
- [ ] **Function names match filenames in PascalCase**
- [ ] Registry entries updated in `_registry.ts`
- [ ] All imports use `~/registry/` or `~/components/` prefix
- [ ] Named exports for all example functions
- [ ] Alert components use `<Alert.Root>` with `<AlertIcon />`
- [ ] Component and prop references use `{:tsx}` syntax in prose
- [ ] **Run `bun run registry:validate` - all checks pass**
- [ ] **Run `bun run registry:build` - registry rebuilt**

# collapsible.mdx

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/collapsible.mdx

title: Collapsible
description: An interactive component which expands/collapses a panel.
  docs: https://react-aria.adobe.com/Disclosure

<ComponentPreview name="collapsible-demo" />

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/collapsible
```

<ComponentSource name="collapsible" />

## Anatomy

  <Tabs.Trigger id="single">Single import</Tabs.Trigger>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="multiple">Multiple imports</Tabs.Trigger>
<Tabs.Content id="single">

```tsx
import { Collapsible } from "~/components/ui/collapsible";

<Collapsible.Root>
  <Collapsible.Trigger>Is it accessible?</Collapsible.Trigger>
  <Collapsible.Content>
    Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.
  </Collapsible.Content>
</Collapsible.Root>;
```

<Tabs.Content id="multiple">

```tsx
import {
  CollapsibleContent,
  CollapsibleRoot,
  CollapsibleTrigger,
} from "~/components/ui/collapsible";

<CollapsibleRoot>
  <CollapsibleTrigger>Is it accessible?</CollapsibleTrigger>
  <CollapsibleContent>
    Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.
  </CollapsibleContent>
</CollapsibleRoot>;
```

## Trigger

You can use the `<Collapsible.Trigger />{:tsx}` component to create a button that toggles the visibility of the collapsible content,
or you can use the `<Button />{:tsx}` component as the trigger by passing it a `slot="trigger"{:tsx}` prop.

```tsx
<Collapsible.Root>
  {/* [!code highlight] */}
  <Button slot="trigger" variant="ghost">
    Is it accessible?
  </Button>
  <Collapsible.Content>
    Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.
  </Collapsible.Content>
</Collapsible.Root>
```

## Animation

The accordion uses the `--disclosure-panel-height{:css}` CSS variable to animate the height of the content area.

      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether the disclosure is disabled.",

      typeSimple: "ReactNode",

title: Dialog
description: A window overlaid on either the primary window or another dialog window, rendering the content underneath inert.
  docs: https://react-aria.adobe.com/Modal

<ComponentPreview name="dialog-demo" />

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/dialog
```

<ComponentSource name="dialog" />

## Anatomy

  <Tabs.Trigger id="single">Single import</Tabs.Trigger>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="multiple">Multiple imports</Tabs.Trigger>
<Tabs.Content id="single">

```tsx
import { Button } from "~/components/ui/button";
import { Dialog } from "~/components/ui/dialog";

<Dialog.Root>
  <Button>Trigger</Button>

  <Dialog.Overlay>
    <Dialog.Modal>
      <Dialog.Content>
        <Dialog.Header>
          <Dialog.Title />
          <Dialog.Description />
        </Dialog.Header>

        <Dialog.Footer>
          <Button slot="close" />
        </Dialog.Footer>

        <Dialog.Close />
      </Dialog.Content>
    </Dialog.Modal>
  </Dialog.Overlay>
</Dialog.Root>;
```

<Tabs.Content id="multiple">

```tsx
import { Button } from "~/components/ui/button";
import {
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogModal,
  DialogOverlay,
  DialogRoot,
  DialogTitle,
} from "~/components/ui/dialog";

<DialogRoot>
  <Button>Trigger</Button>

  <DialogOverlay>
    <DialogModal>
      <DialogContent>
        <DialogHeader>
          <DialogTitle />
          <DialogDescription />
        </DialogHeader>

        <DialogFooter>
          <Button slot="close" />
        </DialogFooter>

        <DialogClose />
      </DialogContent>
    </DialogModal>
  </DialogOverlay>
</DialogRoot>;
```

## Examples

### Scrollable

<ComponentPreview name="dialog-scrollable-demo" />

### Alert Dialog

Use the `role="alertdialog"{:tsx}` prop on the `<Dialog.Content>{:tsx}` element to make an alert dialog.
Also, make sure to set the `isDismissable` prop to `false{:ts}` on the `<Dialog.Overlay>{:tsx}` or `<Dialog.Modal>{:tsx}`
to prevent the dialog from being dismissed by clicking outside of it.

<ComponentPreview name="alert-dialog-demo" />

```tsx
// [!code word:isDismissable={false}]
// [!code word:role="alertdialog"]
<Dialog.Root>
  <Button>Trigger</Button>

  <Dialog.Overlay isDismissable={false}>
    <Dialog.Modal>
      <Dialog.Content role="alertdialog">
        ...
      </Dialog.Content>
    </Dialog.Modal>
  </Dialog.Overlay>
</Dialog.Root>
```

### Sheet

If you need a dialog that slides in from the edge of the screen, check out the [Sheet](/docs/components/sheet) component.

# field.mdx

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/field.mdx

title: Field
description: Combine labels, controls, and help text to compose accessible form fields.

<ComponentPreview name="field-demo" />

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/field
```

<ComponentSource name="field" />

## Anatomy

  <Tabs.Trigger id="single">Single import</Tabs.Trigger>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="multiple">Multiple imports</Tabs.Trigger>
<Tabs.Content id="single">

```tsx
import { Field } from "~/components/ui/field";

<Field.Set>
  <Field.Legend>Profile</Field.Legend>
  <Field.Group>
    <Field.Root>
      <Field.Label>Label</Field.Label>
      {/* Input, Select, Switch, etc. */}
      <Field.Description>Optional helper text.</Field.Description>
      <Field.Error>Validation message.</Field.Error>
    </Field.Root>
  </Field.Group>
</Field.Set>;
```

<Tabs.Content id="multiple">

```tsx
import {
  FieldDescription,
  FieldError,
  FieldGroup,
  FieldLabel,
  FieldLegend,
  FieldRoot,
  FieldSet,
} from "~/components/ui/field";

<FieldSet>
  <FieldLegend>Profile</FieldLegend>
  <FieldGroup>
    <FieldRoot>
      <FieldLabel>Label</FieldLabel>
      {/* Input, Select, Switch, etc. */}
      <FieldDescription>Optional helper text.</FieldDescription>
      <FieldError>Validation message.</FieldError>
    </FieldRoot>
  </FieldGroup>
</FieldSet>;
```

### Structure

- `<Field.Root>{:tsx}` is the core wrapper for a single field.
- `<Field.Content>{:tsx}` is a flex column that groups label and description. Not required if you have no description.
- Wrap related fields with `<Field.Group>{:tsx}`, and use `<Field.Set>{:tsx}` with `<Field.Legend>{:tsx}` for semantic grouping.

## Form

See the [Forms](/docs/forms) documentation for building forms with the Field component and [TanStack Form](/docs/forms/tanstack-form) or [React Hook Form](/docs/forms/react-hook-form).

## Examples

### Input

Use `<Field.Root>{:tsx}` with the `render{:tsx}` prop to compose with `<TextField>{:tsx}` for automatic accessibility wiring.

<ComponentPreview name="field-input-demo" />

### Without TextField

You can use `<Field.Root>{:tsx}` with `<Input>{:tsx}` directly, but you must provide `htmlFor{:tsx}` on the label and `id{:tsx}` on the input manually.

```tsx
<Field.Root>
  <Field.Label htmlFor="email">Email</Field.Label>
  <Input id="email" placeholder="Email" />
</Field.Root>
```

<Alert.Root variant="warning">
  <AlertIcon variant="warning" className="size-4" />
  <Alert.Title>Manual ID wiring</Alert.Title>
  <Alert.Description>
    Without TextField, you lose React Aria's automatic ID association for label,
    description, and error elements. Use `<TextField>{:tsx}` when accessibility is
    critical.
  </Alert.Description>
</Alert.Root>

### Textarea

<ComponentPreview name="field-textarea-demo" />

### Select

<ComponentPreview name="field-select-demo" />

### Checkbox

<ComponentPreview name="field-checkbox-demo" />

### Radio Group

<ComponentPreview name="field-radio-demo" />

### Switch

<ComponentPreview name="field-switch-demo" />

### Fieldset

Use `<Field.Set>{:tsx}` and `<Field.Legend>{:tsx}` for semantic grouping of related fields.

<ComponentPreview name="field-fieldset-demo" />

### Field Group

Stack `<Field.Root>{:tsx}` components with `<Field.Group>{:tsx}`. Add `<Field.Separator>{:tsx}` to divide them.

<ComponentPreview name="field-group-demo" />

## Responsive Layout

- **Vertical fields:** Default orientation stacks label, control, and helper text—ideal for mobile-first layouts.
- **Horizontal fields:** Set `orientation="horizontal"{:tsx}` on `<Field.Root>{:tsx}` to align the label and control side-by-side. Pair with `<Field.Content>{:tsx}` to keep descriptions aligned.
- **Responsive fields:** Set `orientation="responsive"{:tsx}` for automatic column layouts inside container-aware parents.

<ComponentPreview name="field-responsive-demo" />

## Validation and Errors

When using `<Field.Root>{:tsx}` with React Aria field components like `<TextField>{:tsx}`, `<NumberField>{:tsx}`, `<DateField>{:tsx}`, `<ColorField>{:tsx}`, or `<Select>{:tsx}`, pass `isInvalid{:tsx}` to the field component—it handles the invalid state automatically:

```tsx
<Field.Root render={<TextField isInvalid />}>
  <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
  <Input />
  <Field.Error>Enter a valid email address.</Field.Error>
</Field.Root>
```

If you're not using React Aria field components, you must handle validation state manually:

- Add `data-invalid{:tsx}` to `<Field.Root>{:tsx}` to switch the entire block into an error state.
- Add `aria-invalid{:tsx}` on the input itself for assistive technologies.
- Render `<Field.Error>{:tsx}` immediately after the control or inside `<Field.Content>{:tsx}` to keep error messages aligned with the field.

```tsx
<Field.Root data-invalid>
  <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
  <Input aria-invalid />
  <Field.Error>Enter a valid email address.</Field.Error>
</Field.Root>
```

## Accessibility

- `<Field.Set>{:tsx}` and `<Field.Legend>{:tsx}` keep related controls grouped for keyboard and assistive tech users.
- `<Field.Root>{:tsx}` outputs `role="group"{:tsx}` so nested controls inherit labeling from `<Field.Label>{:tsx}` and `<Field.Legend>{:tsx}` when combined.
- When using `<Field.Root>{:tsx}` with `render={<TextField />}{:tsx}`, React Aria automatically associates label, description, and error elements via `aria-labelledby{:tsx}` and `aria-describedby{:tsx}`.

## API Reference

### Field.Set

Container that renders a semantic `fieldset` with spacing presets.

      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes to apply.",

### Field.Legend

Legend element for a `<Field.Set>{:tsx}`. Switch to the `label{:tsx}` variant to align with label sizing.

      name: "variant",
      typeSimple: "enum",
      type: '"legend" | "label"',
      default: '"legend"',
      description: "Visual style variant for the legend.",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes to apply.",

### Field.Group

Layout wrapper that stacks `<Field.Root>{:tsx}` components and enables container queries for responsive orientations.

      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes to apply.",

### Field.Root

The core wrapper for a single field. Provides orientation control, invalid state styling, and spacing.

      name: "orientation",
      typeSimple: "enum",
      type: '"vertical" | "horizontal" | "responsive"',
      default: '"vertical"',
      description: "Layout orientation for the field.",
      name: "render",
      typeSimple: "ReactElement",
      description: "React Aria component to compose with (e.g., TextField).",
      name: "data-invalid",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Marks the field as invalid for manual validation.",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes to apply.",

Use the `render{:tsx}` prop to compose with React Aria components like `<TextField>{:tsx}`:

```tsx
<Field.Root render={<TextField type="email" isRequired />}>
  <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
  <Input />
</Field.Root>
```

### Field.Content

Flex column that groups control and descriptions when the label sits beside the control.

      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes to apply.",

### Field.Label

Label styled for both direct inputs and nested `Field.Root` children.

      name: "htmlFor",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "ID of the form element to associate with.",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes to apply.",

### Field.Title

Renders a title with label styling inside `<Field.Content>{:tsx}`.

      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes to apply.",

### Field.Description

Helper text slot. Uses React Aria's `<Text>{:tsx}` component with `slot="description"{:tsx}`.

      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes to apply.",

### Field.Separator

Visual divider to separate sections inside a `<Field.Group>{:tsx}`. Accepts optional inline content.

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "Optional inline content to display within the separator.",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes to apply.",

```tsx
<Field.Separator>Or continue with</Field.Separator>
```

### Field.Error

Accessible error container that accepts children or an `errors{:tsx}` array.

      name: "errors",
      typeSimple: "array",
      type: "Array<{ message?: string } | undefined>",
      description: "Array of error objects to display.",
      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "Custom error content to display.",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes to apply.",

When the `errors{:tsx}` array contains multiple messages, the component renders a list automatically.

```tsx
<Field.Error
  errors={[{ message: "Required" }, { message: "Invalid format" }]}
/>
```

# form.mdx

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/form.mdx

title: Form
description: A form component that coordinates submission and validation.
  docs: https://react-aria.adobe.com/Form

<Alert.Root>
  <AlertIcon className="size-4" />
  <Alert.Description>
    Form is a **client-only adapter** around React Aria Components. It exists
    to: - Explicitly define a client boundary (`"use client"`) - Isolate React
    Aria as an implementation detail - Provide a stable public API and
    consistent developer experience **Form is a minimal, non-visual coordination
    layer.** It handles submission and validation but does not manage field
    state or control layout. For field composition, use
    [Field](/docs/components/field). See the [Forms architecture
    overview](/docs/forms) to understand the complete system.
  </Alert.Description>
</Alert.Root>

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/form
```

<ComponentSource name="form" />

## Overview

Form is a **minimal, non-visual** component that coordinates:

- Form submission via `onSubmit`
- Server-side validation errors via `validationErrors`
- Reset handling via `onReset`

Form does **not**:

- Manage field state
- Control layout
- Replace the [Field](/docs/components/field) component
- Render visual elements or field containers

For layout and field composition, use the [Field](/docs/components/field) component.

### Understanding the architecture

Form is **only** responsible for submission and validation coordination. It does not handle:

- Individual field layout → Use [Field](/docs/components/field)
- Input behavior and accessibility → Use [TextField](/docs/components/textfield) or similar
- Complex form state → See [Forms overview](/docs/forms) for library integrations

**Recommended reading:**

- [Forms architecture overview](/docs/forms) – Complete explanation of the three-layer system
- [Field documentation](/docs/components/field) – The composition root for all form fields

## Anatomy

```tsx
import { Button } from "~/components/ui/button";
import { Field } from "~/components/ui/field";
import { Form } from "~/components/ui/form";
import { Input } from "~/components/ui/input";
import { TextField } from "~/components/ui/text-field";

<Form>
  <Field.Root render={<TextField name="email" isRequired />}>
    <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
    <Input />
    <Field.Error />
  </Field.Root>
  <Button type="submit">Submit</Button>
</Form>;
```

## Form Libraries

For complex forms with client-side validation and state management, see the [Forms](/docs/forms) guide:

- [TanStack Form](/docs/forms/tanstack-form) - Headless form state management
- [React Hook Form](/docs/forms/react-hook-form) - Performance-focused forms
- [React Aria](/docs/forms/react-aria) - Native HTML validation

## Examples

### Basic

<ComponentPreview name="textfield-form" />

### Server Validation

Use the `validationErrors` prop to display server-side validation errors.

```tsx
<Form validationErrors={{ email: "This email is already registered." }}>
  <Field.Root render={<TextField name="email" />}>
    <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
    <Input />
    <Field.Error />
  </Field.Root>
</Form>
```

### Reset

```tsx
<Form onReset={() => console.log("Form reset")}>
  <Field.Root render={<TextField name="email" />}>
    <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
    <Input />
  </Field.Root>
  <Button type="submit">Submit</Button>
  <Button type="reset" variant="outline">
    Reset
  </Button>
</Form>
```

## API Reference

Form accepts all props from React Aria's [Form](https://react-aria.adobe.com/Form#api).

      name: "validationErrors",
      typeSimple: "object",
      type: "Record<string, string | string[]>",
      description: "Server-side validation errors.",
      name: "validationBehavior",
      typeSimple: "enum",
      type: '"native" | "aria"',
      default: '"native"',
      description: "How validation errors are displayed.",
      name: "onSubmit",
      typeSimple: "function",
      type: "(e: FormEvent) => void",
      description: "Called when form is submitted.",
      name: "onReset",
      typeSimple: "function",
      type: "(e: FormEvent) => void",
      description: "Called when form is reset.",
      name: "onInvalid",
      typeSimple: "function",
      type: "(e: FormEvent) => void",
      description: "Called when form has validation errors.",

## Field Examples

See the following components for form integration examples:

- [Checkbox](/docs/components/checkbox)
- [Date Field](/docs/components/date-field)
- [Radio Group](/docs/components/radio-group)
- [Select](/docs/components/select)
- [Switch](/docs/components/switch)
- [Textarea](/docs/components/textarea)
- [TextField](/docs/components/textfield)

      description: "Additional CSS classes for the root container.",

### InputGroup.Addon

Displays icons, text, buttons, or other content alongside inputs.

<Alert.Root>
  <AlertIcon variant="info" />
  <Alert.Description>
    For proper focus navigation, the `InputGroup.Addon` component should be
    placed after the input. Set the `align` prop to position the addon.
  </Alert.Description>

      name: "align",
      typeSimple: "enum",
      type: '"inline-start" | "inline-end" | "block-start" | "block-end"',
      default: '"inline-start"',
      description: "The position of the addon relative to the input.",
      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The content of the addon (icons, text, buttons).",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the addon.",

For `InputGroup.Input`, use the `inline-start` or `inline-end` alignment. For `InputGroup.Textarea`, use the `block-start` or `block-end` alignment.

### InputGroup.Button

Displays buttons within input groups.

      name: "size",
      typeSimple: "enum",
      type: '"xs" | "icon-xs" | "sm" | "icon-sm"',
      default: '"xs"',
      description: "The size of the button.",
      name: "variant",
      typeSimple: "enum",

      default: '"ghost"',

      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the button.",

### InputGroup.Text

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The text content to display.",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the text.",

### InputGroup.Input

Replacement for `Input` when building input groups. Has input group styles pre-applied.

      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the input.",

All other props are passed through to the underlying `Input` component.

### InputGroup.Textarea

Replacement for `Textarea` when building input groups. Has textarea group styles pre-applied.

      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the textarea.",

All other props are passed through to the underlying `Textarea` component.

# pagination.mdx

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/pagination.mdx

title: Pagination
description: Pagination with page navigation, next and previous links, and arrow key support.
  docs: https://react-aria.adobe.com/Toolbar

<ComponentPreview name="pagination-demo" />

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/pagination
```

<ComponentSource name="pagination" />

## Anatomy

  <Tabs.Trigger id="single">Single import</Tabs.Trigger>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="multiple">Multiple imports</Tabs.Trigger>
<Tabs.Content id="single">

```tsx
import { Pagination } from "~/components/ui/pagination";

<Pagination.Root>
  <Pagination.Content>
    <Pagination.Item>
      <Pagination.Previous href="#" />
    </Pagination.Item>
    <Pagination.Item>
      <Pagination.Link href="#">1</Pagination.Link>
    </Pagination.Item>
    <Pagination.Item>
      <Pagination.Ellipsis />
    </Pagination.Item>
    <Pagination.Item>
      <Pagination.Next href="#" />
    </Pagination.Item>
  </Pagination.Content>
</Pagination.Root>;
```

<Tabs.Content id="multiple">

```tsx
import {
  PaginationRoot,
  PaginationContent,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationPrevious,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationEllipsis,
} from "~/components/ui/pagination";

<PaginationRoot>
  <PaginationContent>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationPrevious href="#" />
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationLink href="#">1</PaginationLink>
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationEllipsis />
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationNext href="#" />
    </PaginationItem>
  </PaginationContent>
</PaginationRoot>;
```

## Examples

### Simple

Only page number links without previous and next navigation.

<ComponentPreview name="pagination-simple-demo" />

### Icons Only

Use `<Pagination.Link>{:tsx}` with icon children and `size="icon"{:tsx}` for compact navigation controls.

<ComponentPreview name="pagination-icons-only-demo" />

## API Reference

### Pagination.Root

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The pagination content.",

### Pagination.Content

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The pagination items.",

### Pagination.Item

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The pagination item content.",

### Pagination.Link

      name: "href",
      required: true,
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "The URL that the link points to.",
      name: "isActive",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      default: "false",
      description:
        "Whether the link represents the current page. Sets aria-current=\"page\" and applies the outline variant.",
      name: "size",
      typeSimple: "enum",
      type: '"default" | "sm" | "lg" | "icon" | "icon-sm" | "icon-lg"',
      default: '"icon"',
      description: "The size of the link button.",

### Pagination.Previous

      name: "href",
      required: true,
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "The URL that the link points to.",

### Pagination.Next

      name: "href",
      required: true,
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "The URL that the link points to.",

### Pagination.Ellipsis

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description:
        "Custom ellipsis content. Defaults to a horizontal dots icon.",

## Changelog

### 2025-02-13

- Wrapped `Pagination.Content` with React Aria [`Toolbar`](https://react-aria.adobe.com/Toolbar) for arrow key navigation between pagination items (single tab stop).
- `Pagination.Content` now accepts `ToolbarProps` from `react-aria-components` instead of `React.ComponentProps<"ul">`.

# resizable.mdx

<ComponentPreview name="resizable-demo" />

## About

The Resizable component is built using the [react-resizable-panels](https://github.com/bvaughn/react-resizable-panels) library.

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/resizable
```

<Step>Install the following dependencies:</Step>

```bash
npm install react-resizable-panels
```

<ComponentSource name="resizable" />

## Anatomy

```tsx
import { Resizable } from "~/components/ui/resizable";

<Resizable.Root orientation="horizontal">
  <Resizable.Panel />
  <Resizable.Separator />
  <Resizable.Panel />
</Resizable.Root>;
```

## Examples

### Vertical

Use the `orientation{:tsx}` prop to set the orientation of the resizable panels.

<ComponentPreview name="resizable-vertical-demo" />

```tsx
// [!code word:orientation]
<Resizable.Root orientation="vertical">
  <Resizable.Panel />
  <Resizable.Separator />
  <Resizable.Panel />
</Resizable.Root>
```

### Handle

Add `<Resizable.Handle>{:tsx}` inside `<Resizable.Separator>{:tsx}` to show a visible drag handle.

<ComponentPreview name="resizable-handle-demo" />

```tsx
// [!code word:Resizable.Handle]
<Resizable.Root>
  <Resizable.Panel />
  <Resizable.Separator>
    <Resizable.Handle />
  </Resizable.Separator>
  <Resizable.Panel />
</Resizable.Root>
```

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/select.mdx

title: Select
description: A select displays a collapsible list of options and allows a user to select one of them.
  docs: https://react-aria.adobe.com/Select

<ComponentPreview name="select-demo" />

## Installation

The Select is built using a composition of the `<Popover />{:tsx}` and the `<Listbox />{:tsx}` components.

See installation instructions for the [Popover](/docs/components/popover#installation) and the [Listbox](/docs/components/list-box#installation) components.

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/select
```

<ComponentSource name="select" />

## Anatomy

  <Tabs.Trigger id="single">Single import</Tabs.Trigger>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="multiple">Multiple imports</Tabs.Trigger>
<Tabs.Content id="single">

```tsx
import { Listbox } from "~/components/ui/list-box";
import { Popover } from "~/components/ui/popover";
import { Select } from "~/components/ui/select";

<Select.Root>
  <Select.Trigger>
    <Select.Value />
  </Select.Trigger>
  <Popover.Content>
    <Listbox.Root>
      <Listbox.Item></Listbox.Item>
    </Listbox.Root>
  </Popover.Content>
</Select.Root>;
```

<Tabs.Content id="multiple">

```tsx
import { ListboxItem, ListboxRoot } from "~/components/ui/list-box";
import { PopoverContent } from "~/components/ui/popover";
import { SelectRoot, SelectTrigger, SelectValue } from "~/components/ui/select";

<SelectRoot>
  <SelectTrigger>
    <SelectValue />
  </SelectTrigger>
  <PopoverContent>
    <ListboxRoot>
      <ListboxItem />
    </ListboxRoot>
  </PopoverContent>
</SelectRoot>;
```

## API Reference

### Select.Root

      name: "selectedKey",
      typeSimple: "Key",
      description: "The currently selected key (controlled).",
      name: "defaultSelectedKey",
      typeSimple: "Key",
      description: "The default selected key (uncontrolled).",
      name: "onSelectionChange",
      typeSimple: "function",
      type: "(key: Key) => void",
      description: "Handler called when the selection changes.",
      name: "isOpen",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether the select is open (controlled).",
      name: "defaultOpen",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether the select is open by default (uncontrolled).",
      name: "onOpenChange",
      typeSimple: "function",
      type: "(isOpen: boolean) => void",
      description: "Handler called when the open state changes.",
      name: "isDisabled",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether the select is disabled.",
      name: "isRequired",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether the select is required.",
      name: "isInvalid",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether the select is invalid.",
      name: "name",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "The name of the select, used when submitting an HTML form.",
      name: "placeholder",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Placeholder text when no item is selected.",

### Select.Trigger

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The trigger content (typically Select.Value).",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the trigger.",

### Select.Value

      name: "placeholder",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Placeholder text when no item is selected.",
      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      type: "ReactNode | (values: SelectValueRenderProps) => ReactNode",
      description: "Custom render for the selected value.",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the value.",

# sheet.mdx

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/sheet.mdx

title: Sheet
description: Extends the Dialog component to display content that complements the main content of the screen.
  docs: https://react-aria.adobe.com/Modal

<ComponentPreview name="sheet-demo" />

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/sheet
```

<ComponentSource name="sheet" />

## Anatomy

  <Tabs.Trigger id="single">Single import</Tabs.Trigger>
  <Tabs.Trigger id="multiple">Multiple imports</Tabs.Trigger>
<Tabs.Content id="single">

```tsx
import { Button } from "~/components/ui/button";
import { Sheet } from "~/components/ui/sheet";

<Sheet.Root>
  <Button>Trigger</Button>

  <Sheet.Overlay>
    <Sheet.Modal>
      <Sheet.Content>
        <Sheet.Header>
          <Sheet.Title />
          <Sheet.Description />
        </Sheet.Header>

        <Sheet.Footer>
          <Button slot="close" />
        </Sheet.Footer>

        <Sheet.Close />
      </Sheet.Content>
    </Sheet.Modal>
  </Sheet.Overlay>
</Sheet.Root>;
```

<Tabs.Content id="multiple">

```tsx
import { Button } from "~/components/ui/button";
import {
  SheetClose,
  SheetContent,
  SheetDescription,
  SheetFooter,
  SheetHeader,
  SheetModal,
  SheetOverlay,
  SheetRoot,
  SheetTitle,
} from "~/components/ui/sheet";

<SheetRoot>
  <Button>Trigger</Button>

  <SheetOverlay>
    <SheetModal>
      <SheetContent>
        <SheetHeader>
          <SheetTitle />
          <SheetDescription />
        </SheetHeader>

        <SheetFooter>
          <Button slot="close" />
        </SheetFooter>

        <SheetClose />
      </SheetContent>
    </SheetModal>
  </SheetOverlay>
</SheetRoot>;
```

## Examples

### Side

Use the `side{:tsx}` prop on `<Sheet.Modal>{:tsx}` to indicate the edge of the screen where the component will appear. The values can be `top{:tsx}`, `right{:tsx}`, `bottom{:tsx}`, or `left{:tsx}`.

<ComponentPreview name="sheet-side-demo" />

## API Reference

### Sheet.Root

      name: "children",
      required: true,
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The trigger and sheet content.",
      name: "isOpen",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether the sheet is open (controlled).",
      name: "defaultOpen",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether the sheet is open by default (uncontrolled).",
      name: "onOpenChange",
      typeSimple: "function",
      type: "(isOpen: boolean) => void",
      description: "Handler called when the open state changes.",

### Sheet.Overlay

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The modal content.",
      name: "isBlurred",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      default: "false",
      description: "Whether the content behind the overlay should be blurred.",
      name: "isDismissable",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      default: "true",
      description: "Whether the sheet can be dismissed by clicking the overlay.",
      name: "isKeyboardDismissDisabled",
      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether pressing the escape key to close the sheet is disabled.",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the overlay.",

### Sheet.Modal

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The sheet content.",
      name: "side",
      typeSimple: "enum",
      type: '"top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left"',
      default: '"right"',
      description: "The side of the screen where the sheet will appear.",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the modal.",

### Sheet.Content

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The content of the sheet.",
      name: "role",
      typeSimple: "enum",
      type: '"dialog" | "alertdialog"',
      default: '"dialog"',
      description: "The role of the sheet.",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the content.",

### Sheet.Header

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The header content (title, description).",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the header.",

### Sheet.Title

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The title text.",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the title.",

### Sheet.Description

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The description text.",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the description.",

### Sheet.Footer

      name: "children",
      typeSimple: "ReactNode",
      description: "The footer content (actions, buttons).",
      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the footer.",

### Sheet.Close

      name: "className",
      typeSimple: "string",
      description: "Additional CSS classes for the close button.",

```tsx
import { Table } from "~/components/ui/table";

<Table.Root>
  <Table.Caption>A list of your recent invoices.</Table.Caption>
  <Table.Header>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Head className="w-[100px]">Invoice</Table.Head>
      <Table.Head>Status</Table.Head>
      <Table.Head>Method</Table.Head>
      <Table.Head className="text-right">Amount</Table.Head>
    </Table.Row>
  </Table.Header>
  <Table.Body>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Cell className="font-medium">INV001</Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell>Paid</Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell>Credit Card</Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell className="text-right">$250.00</Table.Cell>
    </Table.Row>
  </Table.Body>
  <Table.Footer>
    <Table.Row>
      <Table.Cell colSpan={3}>Total</Table.Cell>
      <Table.Cell className="text-right">$2,500.00</Table.Cell>
    </Table.Row>
  </Table.Footer>
</Table.Root>;
```

## API Reference

### Tabs.Root

      name: "selectedKey",
      typeSimple: "Key",
      description: "The currently selected tab key (controlled).",
      name: "defaultSelectedKey",
      typeSimple: "Key",
      description: "The default selected tab key (uncontrolled).",
      name: "onSelectionChange",
      typeSimple: "function",
      type: "(key: Key) => void",
      description: "Handler called when the selected tab changes.",
      name: "orientation",
      typeSimple: "enum",
      type: '"horizontal" | "vertical"',
      default: '"horizontal"',

      typeSimple: "boolean",
      description: "Whether all tabs are disabled.",

# textfield.mdx

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/textfield.mdx

title: TextField
description: A text field allows a user to enter a plain text value with a keyboard.
  docs: https://react-aria.adobe.com/TextField

<Alert.Root>
  <AlertIcon className="size-4" />
  <Alert.Description>
    TextField is a **client-only adapter** around React Aria Components. It
    exists to: - Explicitly define a client boundary (`"use client"`) - Isolate
    React Aria as an implementation detail - Provide a stable public API and
    consistent developer experience **TextField is not meant to be used
    directly.** It should be composed into [Field](/docs/components/field) for
    proper layout and structure. See the [Forms architecture
    overview](/docs/forms) to understand how TextField, Field, and Form work
    together.
  </Alert.Description>
</Alert.Root>

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/text-field
```

<ComponentSource name="text-field" />

## Overview

TextField is a **behavior and accessibility layer** built on React Aria. It is not a visual component—it provides:

- Automatic ID wiring between label, input, description, and error
- Validation state management
- Keyboard and focus handling
- ARIA attributes for screen readers

TextField is designed to be composed **into** the [Field](/docs/components/field) component, which handles layout and visual structure.

### Before you start

TextField is **not responsible for**:

- Layout or visual structure
- Rendering labels, descriptions, or error messages
- Styling or positioning

For complete form fields, use [Field](/docs/components/field) as your composition root. TextField handles behavior; Field handles presentation.

**Recommended reading:**

- [Field documentation](/docs/components/field) – Learn about the composition root
- [Forms architecture overview](/docs/forms) – Understand how all pieces fit together

## Anatomy

TextField wraps your input and connects it to Field's label, description, and error elements.

```tsx
import { Field } from "~/components/ui/field";
import { Input } from "~/components/ui/input";
import { TextField } from "~/components/ui/text-field";

<Field.Root render={<TextField type="email" />}>
  <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
  <Input placeholder="john@example.com" />
  <Field.Description>We'll never share your email.</Field.Description>
  <Field.Error />
</Field.Root>;
```

The `render` prop on `Field.Root` accepts the TextField component. This pattern allows Field to provide layout while TextField provides behavior.

## Accessibility

When TextField is composed with Field:

- `Field.Label` is automatically associated via `aria-labelledby`
- `Field.Description` is associated via `aria-describedby`
- `Field.Error` is associated via `aria-describedby` when invalid
- Focus management and keyboard navigation are handled automatically

### Without TextField

If you use `Field.Root` with `Input` directly (without TextField), you must manually wire IDs:

```tsx
<Field.Root>
  <Field.Label htmlFor="email">Email</Field.Label>
  <Input id="email" aria-describedby="email-desc" />
  <Field.Description id="email-desc">Helper text</Field.Description>
</Field.Root>
```

This approach loses React Aria's automatic association and is not recommended for production forms.

# toast.mdx

Source: https://github.com/fellipeutaka/kanpeki/blob/main/apps/www/src/content/docs/components/toast.mdx

title: Toast
description: A succinct message that is displayed temporarily.
  docs: https://sonner.emilkowal.ski

## Installation

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @kanpeki/toast
```

<Step>Install the following dependencies:</Step>

```bash
npm install next-themes sonner
```

<ComponentSource name="toast" />

<Step>Add the Toaster component</Step>

```tsx title="src/app/providers.tsx"
"use client";

import { ThemeProvider } from "next-themes";
import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";
import { RouterProvider } from "react-aria-components";
import { Toaster } from "~/components/ui/toast"; // [!code highlight]

declare module "react-aria-components" {
  interface RouterConfig {
    routerOptions: NonNullable<
      Parameters<ReturnType<typeof useRouter>["push"]>[1]
    >;
  }
}

interface ProvidersProps {
  children: React.ReactNode;
}

export function Providers({ children }: ProvidersProps) {
  const router = useRouter();

  return (
    <ThemeProvider
      attribute="class"
      defaultTheme="system"
      enableSystem
      disableTransitionOnChange
    >
      <RouterProvider navigate={router.push}>
        {children}
        {/* [!code highlight] */}
        <Toaster />
      </RouterProvider>
    </ThemeProvider>
  );
}
```

## Anatomy

```tsx
import { toast } from "sonner";

toast("Hello, World!", {
  description: "This is a toast message.",
});
```

### Toast Types

```tsx
import { toast } from "sonner";

// Default
toast("Default toast");

// Success
toast.success("Success toast");

// Error
toast.error("Error toast");

// Warning
toast.warning("Warning toast");

// Info
toast.info("Info toast");

// Loading
toast.loading("Loading...");

// Promise
toast.promise(promise, {
  loading: "Loading...",
  success: "Success!",
  error: "Error!",
});

// Custom
toast.custom((t) => <CustomToast id={t} />);
```
